 Centene, Oscar Health outline 2027 ACA marketplace plans
 By
 Paige Minemyer 
 Oct 20, 2026 3:13pm 
 Affordable Care Act (ACA) 
 Oscar Health 
 Centene Corporation 
 Open Enrollment 
 -->
 Here's a look at what some of the leaders in the exchange market will offer in 2027. (tumsasedgars/Getty Images)
 Open enrollment for the Affordable Care Act's marketplaces opens on Nov. 1, and with more turbulence on deck, insurers are offering a look at their plans for the coming year.
 An August analysis from KFF found a median premium increase of 15% in 2027 . That comes as insurers navigate the ongoing impacts of the expiration of the enhanced premium tax credits alongside significant changes implemented through multiple federal program integrity rules.
 Those rules have faced legal challenges, but plans have still needed to account for the changes included therein. KFF said that the 15% increase makes for the second year in a row with a double-digit median increase. For 2025, the median proposed increase was 18%.
 With that backdrop, here's a look at what some of the leaders in the exchange market will offer in 2027.
 Related
 Moody's: A look at payers' 'diverging' paths for MA, ACA markets 
 Centene Corporation
 Centene's Ambetter Health unit, the brand for its marketplace plans, will expand into 55 new counties for the 2027 plan year, the company announced . Ambetter currently covers about 3.5 million people across 27 states and 1,700 counties.
 The company will add a mix of new, condition-specific plans under the Ambetter Health Premier umbrella, including plans in North Carolina and Ohio that target patients with congestive heart failure. Members that enroll in these plans will see $0 copayments for certain heart failure medications as well as up to four $0 cardiologist visits per year.
 The plans also include $0 copayments for certain mental health medications and nicotine replacement therapy, as well as coverage for key cholesterol labs, EKGs, cardiac education programs and nutritional counseling.
 In addition to the new plans, Ambetter is expanding the reach of existing plans for individuals with diabetes and asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The diabetes care plans are currently available in Florida, Tennessee, Texas, Alabama and Oklahoma, and Centene will add Louisiana, Mississippi and Indiana for 2027.
 In these plans, members can access $0 preferred insulin as well as $0 copayments for certain medications for managing diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol and mental health conditions. The plans also offer no costs for certain diabetes supplies and routine A1C lab services.
 The plans for asthma and COPD, meanwhile, include $0 copays for preferred asthma or COPD medications, pulmonology visits, allergy tests and pulmonary rehabilitation services.
 In Ambetter's traditional plans, members can access virtual care around the clock, and in participating states, the My Health Pays rewards program that offers annual rewards for completing certain health challenges.
 "We are committed to delivering coverage options that reflect the diverse healthcare needs of the communities we serve," said Katherine Kirby, president of Ambetter Health, in the announcement. "Our condition-specific plans have delivered strong member satisfaction and primary care engagement, demonstrating the value of more personalized approaches to coverage." 
 Oscar Health
 Oscar Health will offer plans in 713 counties across 21 states for 2027, a 24% increase in the number of counties it serves, per an announcement .
 A new offering for the coming year is a plan called RetireEase, which aims to support the transition from early retirement to Medicare enrollment. The plan will be available in five states: Arizona, Florida, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas.
 Under this plan, members can continue to see their trusted providers, and will see set prices for key services like preventive care, labs, physical therapy, heart care and bone-and-joint care. The plan includes no cost generic medications and supports for caregiving, transportation and the transition to Medicare.
 The company is also expanding existing plans that target particular life stages or conditions. For example, the HelloMeno plan, which is designed for women navigating menopause, will grow to 15 states. In this plans, members can access a $0 package of key services including hormone therapy, bone-density scans, insomnia treatment and cancer screenings.
 The insurer's Hy-Vee Health with Oscar, a cobranded offering with Hy-Vee stores, will also add new regions within Iowa and grow into Nebraska, Missouri and Kansas. The plan includes concierge care services and food discounts at Hy-Vee stores.
 In addition, Oscar said it will add more than 250 new plans that include vision and dental services bundled in automatically, including $0 preventative dental visits and eye exams, as well as discounts for vision care.
 Members can also tap into Oscar's rewards program, called Oscar Unlocks.
 "The individual market is built for everyone from entrepreneurs launching businesses to people working part-time to employees and gig workers of companies large and small," said Mark Bertolini, CEO of Oscar Health. "We listen to what they want, what makes their day-to-day easier, and deliver healthcare with intuitive technology that fits their lifestyle."
 "Every Oscar product helps people take control of their health at every stage of life. It's healthcare made-for-me," he said.
